text: {"summary":"Task: repair Python 3.11 resolver via complete replacements for engine.py and rules.py; entrypoint engine.solve(data). No third-party libraries/tools/network/workspace access. Output candidate format has files array for the two allowlisted paths; values/order empty.\nConfirmed requirements through stage 5/8: packages maps names to version rows with deps; roots maps package names to inclusive [min,max]. Install exactly the transitive dependency closure of roots, satisfying all root constraints and every dependency constraint from every selected version. Dependencies may be strings (unbounded) or objects {name,min,max} with optional bounds. Shared constraints must all hold; use backtracking. Candidate must maximize lexicographic version vector over sorted package names, with -1 for absent packages. Return {'error':'unsatisfiable'} if no solution, otherwise {'versions':{name:version,...}}. New stage-5 requirement: data may include blocked mapping package names to forbidden versions; absent entries forbid nothing. Never select blocked versions.\nCurrent checkpoint implementation in supplied history recursively resolves dependencies, accumulates root/dependency range constraints, backtracks, and maximizes the sorted-name version vector; rules.options filters inclusive bounds and sorts descending. It does not yet handle blocked versions, so add that. Public tests have passed through stage 4 (latest recorded feedback 8 checks, public_pass); stage 5 tests are supplied but no result is recorded. Stage 5 examples: b=1 blocked makes solution unsatisfiable in one case; blocking b=2 expects a=1,b=1,c=1. 26 actions remain. Later stages may add requirements. Trial notes are unverified; do not invent a wrong attempt."}
